Measures every cycle whether the battery discharges while power is fed into the grid at the same time. This is almost always wasted stored energy. With a fixed feed-in tariff combined with grid charging of the battery it can also jeopardise the tariff (mixed-storage rules of the Federal Network Agency). The minutes and Wh per day are kept in separate variables and archived. EMS only intervenes when it is driving an active setpoint itself: then EMS falls back to inverter self-regulation after the set time and reports it visibly. The inverter's automatic mode itself, grid operator commands and Tibber Grid Rewards remain untouched.

Only takes effect if the inverter reports the required commands (detected automatically via InverterHub) and EMS has control authority. Otherwise everything stays as before. Price optimisation, Grid Rewards, grid operator commands and battery boost always take precedence.

🌞 Absorb the midday peak: if the forecast PV surplus up to the start of the peak window is certain to fill the battery anyway, EMS blocks charging beforehand. The surplus then goes to the grid. From the peak window on, EMS always releases charging — that is when the battery should charge instead of feeding in additionally (exactly when all PV systems feed into the grid the most). If the purchase price (including conversion and cycle costs) is currently lower than the feed-in tariff, EMS always blocks regardless of the time — buffering does not pay off then, cheap grid purchase later replaces the battery. If the measured PV is no longer safely above the house load, EMS releases immediately. Requires the PV forecast (detected automatically); the load forecast is optional (otherwise an average value).

How does export work when the battery is full?

popup.caption: How does export work when the battery is full?

items.caption: If the battery is full and there is still PV surplus, EMS actively requests export. As target value EMS automatically uses the current PV forecast (module "Prognose"/PVF, if installed) for the current quarter-hour slot — weather-dependent, no manual input required. The inverter's export setpoint mode actively aims at this value and taps the battery if necessary to reach it; a safety exit aborts immediately if the battery state of charge visibly drops below the daily target. Without an installed forecast module this function stays disabled.

When do I need load balancing?

popup.caption: When do I need load balancing?

items.caption: OFF by default (0) -- not needed by everyone. Only relevant if your grid connection/main fuse has a hard limit that could be exceeded by several wallboxes charging at the same time plus base load.

If the limit is exceeded, EMS switches off the wallbox with the lowest priority (see WB{n}_Priority below) until grid import is below the limit again. Protects against a tripped fuse, but does not replace proper protection of the electrical installation.

WebFront/app: for each active wallbox EMS creates the variables "Wallbox n: plan (what happens next)", "Charging mode", "Charging target", "Deadline" and "Command" (charge now for 1 hour, end override, delete charging target). Changing the charging mode, target and deadline there changes these settings here directly (one source). If this form is open at the same time, reload it before "Apply", otherwise it overwrites the change from the WebFront.

Charging target: if a target is set and a vehicle is plugged in, EMS charges the missing kWh in the cheapest quarter-hours until the deadline (with a 20 % time buffer) and overrides the charging mode while doing so. Once the target is reached or the deadline has passed, the charging mode applies again. If the time is not sufficient, EMS charges immediately and warns. Requires a wallbox that reports the energy of the charging session (ChargerHub from 0.9.128). §14a, battery boost and Smart Charging take precedence.

Charging modes only apply if EMS controls the wallbox (not with Smart Charging or Monitor only) and the wallbox accepts a current setpoint. Grid operator blocking (§14a) and battery boost take precedence. PV surplus = PV minus house minus the other wallbox; the battery gets what is left. Charging starts from the minimum current of the wallbox, on/off changes at the earliest after the cooldown, and charging only stops after the cooldown and the minimum charging time.

Requires Tibber (PT15M prices) + battery enabled, PV forecast (PVF) optional. Automatically calculates a plan for the whole day when new prices arrive (charge/discharge/feed-in per quarter-hour) and writes it visibly into the weekly schedule "EMS Tagesplan (automatisch)" below this instance — also at negative prices (always charge) and at prices below the feed-in tariff (the house runs from the grid, the battery is spared).

items.name: PLAN_NightGrid_Active
items.caption: Night window: until the end hour, charge the battery from the grid in the cheapest quarter-hours and supply the house from the grid as long as the grid price is below the feed-in tariff (minus 5 % battery loss)

items.name: PLAN_NightGrid_ExtendHours
items.caption: Extend purchase: keep charging for up to this many hours after the end hour if the battery is not yet full and the price is reasonable (0 = off)

items.name: PLAN_NightGrid_ExtendTol_ct
items.caption: Extend purchase: at most this much more expensive than the cheapest quarter-hour of the window (and below the feed-in tariff)

items.name: PLAN_NightGrid_NeedBased
items.caption: Night window: leave room for the next day's PV surplus (charges up to the night target, minus what PV will safely charge the next day according to the conservative forecast; at least the demand until the next night. Off: always up to the night target)

items.name: PLAN_Restwert_Aktiv
items.caption: Residual value of the battery energy (beta): the battery is spared and the house runs from the grid if the stored energy will earn more later (until the next refill by PV or grid charging) than grid import now, by at least the minimum margin for price arbitrage. Visible in the day plan as hold battery with reasoning. Try it in dry run first for comparison.

items.name: PLAN_Bedarf_Aktiv
items.caption: Demand safeguard: simulates the SOC with the conservative PV forecast (p10) and the load forecast (includes the heat pump via heating degrees and outdoor temperature) until PV takes over the next day. If the energy would not suffice (reserve plus safety margin from the battery panel), the plan buys exactly the missing amount in the cheapest quarter-hours before the shortfall, provided that pays off against the expensive price after conversion losses, cycle costs and minimum margin. At runtime nothing is bought if the real SOC is already above the planned value.

items.name: PLAN_Abend_MinSoc
items.caption: Optional lower limit at the evening hour (0 = off): additionally, the SOC at the evening hour should be at least this high, even if the calculated demand is lower

items.name: PLAN_Abend_Hour
items.caption: Evening hour for the lower limit

Manual entries in the day plan: they take precedence over automatic planning (not over §14a commands of the grid operator and not over Grid Rewards). Date in the format YYYY-MM-DD or DD.MM.YYYY (empty = every day), times as HH:MM (To is exclusive; if it is missing, the entry applies until midnight). Action "Grid charging" charges from the grid (power 0 = as much as possible), "Hold battery" supplies the house from the grid, "Automatic" forces the inverter's automatic mode. Entries with a past date are ignored.

items.name: PLAN_PreDischarge_Active
items.caption: Pre-discharge: empty the battery via the grid before a significantly cheaper night charging window (feed-in from the battery, price-weighted). Only together with the night window.

items.name: PLAN_PreDischarge_MinGain_ct
items.caption: Pre-discharge: minimum profit per kWh after conversion losses (ct, also covers cycle wear)

Caution: pre-discharge feeds battery energy into the grid. With mixed storage systems with a fixed feed-in tariff and grid charging this can jeopardise the tariff (exclusivity, MiSpeL alternative) — only enable it if this has been clarified for your system.

In the day plan the night window appears as "Grid charging" (cheapest quarter-hours, target as for night charging above) and "Hold battery (grid import)" (remaining quarter-hours with a price below 95 % of the feed-in tariff; more expensive quarter-hours are still supplied by the battery). The reasoning per quarter-hour states rank and price. Caution: grid charging has legal consequences for mixed storage systems (feed-in tariff, exclusivity) — only enable it deliberately if this has been clarified for your system.
